# `silk/platform/wasm/thread`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

The wasi-threads records of a multi-threaded wasm32 module.

## When to use
`NativeThread` starts and joins wasm32 threads through [`WasmThread`](#WasmThread). Applications use
`silk.concurrency.thread_native`.

## Details
Each thread owns a record and a 1 MiB stack from the module's heap. The host starts the thread
as a new instance on the shared memory and calls the module's `wasi_thread_start`, which the
compiler defines: it moves the shadow stack to the record's stack top, calls the entry module's
thread entry, then marks the record done and wakes the joiner. The joiner releases the stack and
the record only after it sees the record done, which the thread sets after its last stack use.

Public declarations: 1.

<a id="WasmThread.impl.spawn"></a>

### Associated function `spawn`

```silk
pub unsafe fn spawn(argument: ?*mut u8) -> Result<?[*]mut u8, i32>
```

Starts a thread that runs the entry module's thread entry with `argument`. It returns the
thread's handle, or an error number when the host refuses the thread or the heap is full
(12, `ENOMEM`).

#### Safety
Join each started handle once with [`WasmThread.join`](#WasmThread.impl.join).

<a id="WasmThread.impl.argument"></a>

### Associated function `argument`

#### Safety

### Associated function `done`

```silk
pub unsafe fn done(handle: ?[*]mut u8) -> *mut u32
```

Returns the word that `wasi_thread_start` sets to 1 once the thread's work is over.

#### Safety
`handle` is a live handle from [`WasmThread.spawn`](#WasmThread.impl.spawn).

<a id="WasmThread.impl.join"></a>

### Associated function `join`

```silk
pub unsafe fn join(handle: ?[*]mut u8) -> ()
```

Waits for the thread behind `handle` to finish, then releases its stack and record.

#### Safety
`handle` is a live handle from [`WasmThread.spawn`](#WasmThread.impl.spawn), joined only once.
